title: Tennis Ball Dribble Challenge
description: Players dribble a basketball with one hand while tossing and catching a tennis ball with the other, isolating true one-handed ball control.

content.objective: Prove true one-handed control by removing the usual second-hand assistance.
content.setup: Each player dribbles a basketball with one hand while holding a small tennis-style ball in the other.
instructions: Dribble the basketball with the right hand while tossing the tennis ball up and catching it with the left.
Add a few steps of walking once both hands can manage the pattern.
Finish with eyes closed for five seconds on each hand, if under control.
coachingPoints: Let the dribbling hand work completely independently of the tossing hand.
Keep the basketball dribble at a normal, game-like height.
Reset calmly if control is lost rather than rushing back in.
commonMistakes: Dribbling too low out of caution, which isn't game-realistic.
Watching the dribbling hand instead of the tennis ball.
Letting the off-hand drop instead of staying ready to protect the ball.
content.safety: Use a soft tennis-style ball only, not anything with a hard surface.
